📣 Are you a Cato Podcast listener? We want to hear from you!  

✍️ Please share your thoughts in this 3-minute anonymous survey to help us improve. 

🤩 Thank you for your time and for your continued support! 

➡️ ow.ly/uGmK50Yy3nf

Remembering Brian Doherty, historian of the libertarian movement and editor with @reason magazine. 

“His impact on the libertarian movement and on libertarian ideas is well known, but that’s not all he impacted,” writes Ivan G. Osorio. 

ow.ly/yUZ150Yyl25

Minnesota lawmakers are weighing whether to carve AI out of the free speech protections in their state constitution. It's a troubling sign of state lawmakers responding to AI fears by threatening core liberties, says Cato's @KevinTFrazier. 
ow.ly/yJja50YxPp5

The government loses about 4 cents per dollar on student loans, says Cato’s @Gillen_Andrew_J. It shouldn’t be the lender at all, he adds, but at minimum, it shouldn’t be losing (or making) money on them. 

Learn more: ow.ly/r40950YxQaa

Video

Director of Energy and Environmental Policy Studies at the Cato Institute, @ts_fisher, will testify before the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources on “The State of the Bulk Power System,” Wednesday, March 25, at 9:30 a.m. 

ow.ly/nTXq50YykEI

Moving student loans to the Treasury Department puts finance where it belongs and makes it easier to phase out the Department of Education, says Cato’s @Gillen_Andrew_J. A smaller federal footprint will provide more room for states to shape education in their own way. 

ow.ly/Hweu50Yy6ff

Obamacare is 16. Despite promising affordability, it has doubled premiums for most consumers and eroded choice of treatments and providers. Obamacare relief would offer comprehensive coverage at lower premiums, says Cato’s @mfcannon. 

cato.org/blog/obamacare-16-t…

📚 Join Cato University in Phoenix on April 18 for a full day exploring liberty with leading scholars and peers. 

💫 Receive free resources and a $100 travel stipend upon completion. 

❗Space is limited. Apply before the deadline on April 8!

✅ Apply here: ow.ly/wlNn50Yyea1

The government should avoid micromanaging innovation, says Cato’s @kevintfrazier. If America wants to lead in AI, it should ensure market competition and entrepreneurial freedom over regulation.

ow.ly/V3GY50Yy5Qu

Washington knows it has a spending problem. What it lacks is the will, and an effective mechanism, to do something about it, Cato’s @RominaBoccia says.  

A BRAC-like fiscal commission won’t make tough choices easy. But it could finally make them possible. 

ow.ly/qy8b50YxPwr

In his famous “punch bowl” speech, former Fed Chairman William McChesney Martin stressed that the Fed must remove easy money before inflation heats up, safeguard long-term stability, and support a free-market system where individual freedom and responsibility thrive, explains Cato’s James A. Dorn. 
ow.ly/EWV050YxPZo

Immigrants and US sponsors paid over $1 billion in fees for applications the government isn’t processing, per 2024 data, says Cato’s @David_J_Bier. 

“If applicants aren’t eligible, deny them—but don’t take their money and withhold the service,” he adds. 

ow.ly/tYKb50YxPTN

A balanced budget amendment won’t fix our debt crisis by itself, but it could help impose needed fiscal discipline. A new analysis by Cato’s @LettDominik discusses H.J. Res. 139, a balanced budget amendment introduced by Rep. Andy Biggs (R‑AZ).
ow.ly/MCRR50YxP14

The Trump administration unveiled a national AI framework that allocates proper regulatory authority between the federal government and states while also maintaining a light-touch approach, writes Cato's @kevintfrazier. 
ow.ly/A53l50YxPhp

The Pentagon’s new Economic Defense Unit is reportedly recruiting Wall Street talent from firms tied to the industries it may target. Cato’s @DeHavenTad warns this looks less like defense policy and more like a shadow investment fund.
ow.ly/bsos50YxP7A

A 30-day DHS shutdown hasn’t slowed ICE or Border Patrol—nearly $170 billion in funding keeps them running with minimal transparency and oversight. On the latest Cato Podcast, @LettDominik and @David_J_Bier break down what this reveals about Washington’s broken appropriations process. 

Apple Podcasts: ow.ly/fWG350YxHiS
Spotify: ow.ly/MmJ750YxHiR
Website: ow.ly/8soB50YxHiQ

F.A. Hayek (1899-1992), one of the most important free market economists in history, died on March 23, 1992. 

He refuted the tenets of socialism in his best-selling book “The Road to Serfdom,” and was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1974. If you want to fight for freedom, study Hayek.

Trump’s rationales for denying birthright citizenship to children of undocumented immigrants are at odds with the 14th Amendment’s core purpose: granting citizenship to freed slaves and their descendants. The original meaning counts against the administration, reports Cato’s @IlyaSomin. 
ow.ly/Svn850YxIvf
